plan.name: triage-unassigned-bug-issues
plan.title: Triage unassigned bug issues
plan.description: Every weekday at 9am, triage newly reported open bug issues in {{repo}} by asking for reproduction details and version info, then label them {{needs_info_label}}.
plan.summary: Find open, unassigned bug issues in the target repo, ask for repro/version details, and mark them needs-info.
plan.generalization: Generalize the recorded one-off issue triage into a repeatable GitHub CLI workflow: discover every open issue in the target repository that has the bug label and no assignee, skip issues already marked needs-info so reruns stay idempotent, then post the standard follow-up comment and apply the needs-info label to each remaining issue.

values.name: Follow-up comment
values.value: Thanks for the report! Could you share exact reproduction steps and the version you're on?

steps.label: Find triage candidates
steps.prompt: Use `gh issue list -R {{repo}} --state open --label {{bug_label}} --search 'no:assignee -label:"{{needs_info_label}}"'` to list every open issue in {{repo}} that needs triage. If none are found, exit cleanly; otherwise capture the issue numbers and URLs for the next step.

steps.label: Request repro details
steps.prompt: For each candidate issue in {{repo}}, post {{follow_up_comment}} with `gh issue comment`, then add the {{needs_info_label}} label with `gh issue edit --add-label`. Use the issue number or URL from the discovery step, and keep the loop going until every candidate is processed.

plan.description: Every weekday morning, find open pull requests in {{repo}} that have been waiting on review for more than {{review_wait_days}} days and post a gentle reminder comment on each one.
plan.summary: Checks for stale review-needed PRs and nudges each one with a friendly comment.
plan.generalization: The recorded run reviewed one open PR in the GitHub repository and posted a reminder comment because it had been awaiting review for more than two days. Generalize this into a repeatable sweep: list all open PRs that still require review, compute the age cutoff at runtime, and comment on every qualifying PR rather than only the example PR.

values.name: Reminder comment
values.value: Friendly ping — this PR has been waiting on review for a couple of days, could you take a look?

steps.label: Find stale review-needed PRs
steps.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI (`gh`) in PowerShell to list all open pull requests in {{repo}} that still require review and were created before the runtime cutoff for {{review_wait_days}} days ago. Compute the cutoff date at run time, then query with `gh pr list -R {{repo}} --state open --search 'review:required created:<YYYY-MM-DD'` and capture every matching PR number and URL.

steps.label: Post a reminder on each PR
steps.prompt: For each qualifying pull request, post the fixed reminder comment {{reminder_comment}} with `gh pr comment -R {{repo}} <pr-number> --body {{reminder_comment}}`. Keep the action explicit and only comment on PRs that still meet the age and review-required criteria.

plan.name: release-notes-and-deploy
plan.title: Release notes and deploy
plan.description: Compile release notes from a milestone's merged PRs into the CHANGELOG, bump the version, deploy to production, and verify the deployment.
plan.summary: Queries the GitHub milestone for all merged PRs, compiles their titles into the CHANGELOG.md, bumps the package version, commits and pushes, deploys to production via the deploy script, and runs a health check on the live API endpoint.
plan.generalization: The recording acted on one specific milestone (v2.4.0) and copied three PR titles manually. The generalized automation queries ALL merged PRs for a configurable milestone (as a fixed value), extracts their titles programmatically via the gh CLI, and inserts them into CHANGELOG.md. The version bump, deploy, and health check steps are reusable across any release.

steps.label: Pull latest main branch
steps.prompt: Run `git checkout main && git pull` to ensure the local repo is up to date with the remote.

steps.label: Fetch merged PRs for the milestone
steps.prompt: Use `gh pr list -R {{repo}} --state merged --search 'milestone:{{milestone}}' --json number,title --jq '.[].title'` to retrieve all merged PR titles for the {{milestone}} milestone. Store the list in memory for the next step.

steps.label: Add PR titles to CHANGELOG.md
steps.prompt: Read the CHANGELOG.md file in the repo root. Append a new section with today's date and the version milestone, then insert each merged PR title as a bullet point. Save the file.

steps.label: Bump version, commit, and deploy
steps.prompt: Run `npm version {{version_bump_type}}` to bump the version. Then run `git push` to push the version commit and tags. Run `./deploy.sh production` to deploy to the production environment.

steps.label: Health-check the deployed service
steps.prompt: Run `curl -s {{api_health_url}}` to verify the health endpoint is responding. Log the result to confirm the deployment succeeded.

plan.name: azure-webapp-deploy
plan.title: Deploy and verify Azure web app
plan.description: Deploy a Node.js web app to Azure using the CLI, verify it is live at its deployed URL, and record the live site URL in a deployment tracking spreadsheet. Runs on a user-defined schedule (proposed: daily at 9am, 2pm, and 6pm).
plan.summary: Automates Azure CLI deployment of a web app, health-checks the live site, and updates a deployments log with the live URL.
plan.generalization: The recording deployed a single app (contoso-crm) to Azure and logged it. The automation generalizes this into a repeatable procedure: deploy any app by name to a specified resource group, verify it is live by fetching the deployed URL, and append the deployment record (app name, URL, timestamp) to a deployments tracking spreadsheet using the xlsx skill.

steps.label: Deploy the app with Azure CLI
steps.prompt: Ensure you are signed into Azure (run `az login` if needed). Use the Azure CLI to deploy the web app: run `az webapp up --name {{app_name}} --resource-group {{resource_group}} --runtime {{runtime}}` in PowerShell on Windows. Capture the deployment URL from the command output.

steps.label: Verify the live site
steps.prompt: Fetch the deployed app URL (https://{{app_name}}.azurewebsites.net/) to verify the deployment is live and the site responds with a 200 status. If the site is not yet responding, wait a moment and retry.

steps.label: Update the deployments log with xlsx
steps.prompt: Use the xlsx built-in skill to open {{deployments_xlsx}}. Append a new row with: the app name ({{app_name}}), the live URL (https://{{app_name}}.azurewebsites.net/), and the current date and time. Save the updated spreadsheet.
